context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Written things and an uncomprehended saying” preserves a distinct parallel witness source unit within anticipation.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus takes the Twelve, connects what is coming with the prophets, names treatment by Gentiles and death, and the disciples do not understand.
observations.label: Written things and an uncomprehended saying: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps jesus, twelve, prophets visible within its Crucifixion evidence.
observations.label: Written things and an uncomprehended saying: action, promise, or consequence

payload.posture: Read Luke 18:31–34 as its own anticipation and stated approach crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: This witness selects its own people, actions, words, and sequence around the Crucifixion without explaining every difference from the other witnesses.
payload.title: Written things and an uncomprehended saying
